title: Serenade for Strings in C major
hook: A bow to Mozart, a waltz and two Russian folk songs, for strings alone.

painting.title: Moscow Courtyard
painting.pairingNote: A sunlit Moscow courtyard with a church beyond, painted two years before the Serenade; ordinary Russian life in warm, clear light, like the waltz and the folk songs of the finale.

facts: Tchaikovsky wrote the Serenade in September and October 1880, in the same weeks as the *1812* Overture. He told his patroness Nadezhda von Meck that he had composed it “from an innate impulse”, as something he felt deep within himself, and he told his publisher that he loved it “terribly”.
He meant the first movement as an imitation of Mozart’s style. Its title, “piece in the form of a sonatina”, names a small, classical form.
It is for strings only: violins, violas, cellos and double basses. In the score Tchaikovsky asked for as many players as possible.

Teachers and students of the Moscow Conservatory played it to him as a surprise in December 1880. The first public performance was in St Petersburg in October 1881, conducted by Eduard Nápravník. It is dedicated to Karl Albrecht, a cellist who worked at the conservatory.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a grand opening and a light-footed dance in Mozart’s honour (I), a waltz (II), an elegy (III), two Russian folk songs and a return to the start (IV).

movements.heading: Pezzo in forma di sonatina: Andante non troppo – Allegro moderato
movements.tempo: Pezzo in forma di sonatina: Andante non troppo – Allegro moderato
movements.summary: A slow, grand introduction in rich, full chords, then a quick, graceful Allegro. A [[sonatina|sonatina]] is a small sonata: the themes are laid out and then simply come back, with no development in between. At the end, the grand introduction returns to close the movement.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: a slow, falling melody in heavy chords, marked *sempre marcatissimo*, always strongly accented.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a light, dancing tune with little gaps in it.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: quick, scurrying notes passed between the sections.

stops.hear: The whole string orchestra plays a slow, solemn melody in thick, rich chords
The melody rises and swells, then settles into a quiet close
Lighter and quicker: a graceful, dancing tune in the violins, with little rests in it
Fast, scurrying notes run from the violins to the violas and cellos
The dancing tune again, as at the start of the Allegro
stops.happening: The return of the themes, without a development in between

stops.hear: The scurrying theme again, now in the home key
The slow, solemn chords of the opening return
stops.happening: The introduction comes back as a [[coda|coda]]

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: A final, heavy C major chord

notice: Listen to the opening chords: the violins and violas play two notes at once ([[double-stop|double stop]]s), which is why the sound is so full.
Notice the gaps in the dancing tune at ≈ 1:50. When the tune returns at ≈ 4:30, are they filled in?

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Karajan recorded the Serenade twice for Deutsche Grammophon with the Berliner Philharmoniker. This is the first, made in Berlin’s Jesus-Christus-Kirche in October 1966; a digital remake followed in 1980. On the Spotify album the Serenade is tracks 4–7, after the *1812* Overture.

movements.heading: Waltz: Moderato – Tempo di valse
movements.summary: A light, elegant [[waltz|waltz]] that became popular on its own; Tchaikovsky often conducted it separately. The first violins have the tune almost throughout, over the classic “one, two, three” with a heavy bass on the first beat.

mainIdeas.name: The waltz tune
mainIdeas.description: a smooth, swaying melody that climbs and floats down again.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: falling phrases in the violins over heavier basses.

stops.hear: A short rising lead-in; then the violins sing a light waltz tune over an “um-pah-pah”
The violins climb high, hold there, and come down
Second violins and cellos take the tune, an octave lower
stops.happening: The tune in a darker colour

stops.hear: The violins play falling phrases again and again; the cellos and basses answer heavily
The waltz tune returns; the low strings now pluck the bass and the violas add a harmony

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The tune drifts down to a gentle close

notice: Listen to the bass on the first beat of each bar: it is what makes the music turn like a dance.
When the tune comes back at ≈ 2:05, the accompaniment is plucked. Compare it with the start.

movements.heading: Élégie: Larghetto elegiaco
movements.summary: An elegy is a song of mourning, but this one is more tender than sad. A slow, mysterious introduction leads to a long melody for the violins over plucked strings. In the middle the music grows darker and more restless; then the melody returns, passed to the violas and then high in the violins.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: upper strings rising while lower strings fall, in quiet, solemn chords.

mainIdeas.name: The main melody
mainIdeas.description: warm and singing, first in the violins.

stops.hear: Slow, quiet chords: the upper strings rise while the lower strings fall; they settle on two D major chords
The violins sing a long, warm melody; the other strings pluck soft broken chords below
stops.happening: The main melody, in D major

stops.hear: Violas and cellos take the melody; the violins weave a second line around it
Darker: a held bass note, the melody turned minor and echoed between violins and cellos, with restless triplets
A climax; then the violas lead a falling line over solid chords
The violas sing the main melody, back in the major
The violins carry the melody very high; the cellos answer with a falling line
The introduction’s chords return, [[muted|muted]] and veiled

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The melody in the minor over the basses’ triplets, then a final rising scale to a high D

notice: In the opening, follow the top and the bottom at the same time: they move in opposite directions.
Listen for the moment the violas take the tune at ≈ 4:30. The viola’s darker, husky sound changes its mood.

movements.heading: Finale (Tema russo): Andante – Allegro con spirito
movements.tempo: Finale (Tema russo): Andante – Allegro con spirito
movements.summary: Two Russian folk songs, both of which Tchaikovsky had arranged in a collection years before. A slow introduction on muted strings quotes “On the Green Meadow”; then the Allegro dances off with “Under the Green Apple Tree”. Near the end the grand introduction of the first movement returns, and turns into the dance tune.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, hymn-like folk song on muted strings.
A second, broad singing tune, first in the cellos.

stops.hear: Muted strings play a slow, gentle tune, softly, like a distant song
stops.happening: The introduction, the folk song “On the Green Meadow”, in G major

stops.hear: The mutes come off and the violins start a quick, bouncing dance in C major
stops.happening: “Under the Green Apple Tree”, *Allegro con spirito*

stops.hear: The cellos sing a broad, bright melody; the violins take it up
The dance tune is passed around, builds to a climax and drops back
The dance from the beginning of the Allegro
The cellos’ broad melody again, now in C major
stops.happening: The second theme in the home key

stops.hear: Suddenly slow and grand: the opening chords of the first movement

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: The solemn chords speed up and turn into the dance tune; a rush to the final C major chords

notice: At ≈ 6:25, listen to how the solemn opening melody runs straight into the folk dance, without a break.
Compare the muted strings at the start with the full sound a minute later.

threads.title: Mozart
threads.body: The first movement imitates Mozart’s style, and the serenade itself was a favourite form of Mozart’s time.

threads.title: Russia
threads.body: The finale is built on two Russian folk songs, which Tchaikovsky had arranged years before.

threads.title: The return
threads.body: The grand opening comes back at the end of the first movement and again at the end of the whole work, tying it together.

threads.title: Strings alone
threads.body: No winds, no brass, no drums: all the colour comes from bowing, plucking and muting.
